capability_investigated: generate() batched per-item prompt-list decode over multiple feature windows, and how window boundaries map back to text seams
what_i_learned: the fixed-30s mel extractor forces any long-form fix to slice audio, and a hard non-overlapping cut leaves each 30s seam decoded by only one window — so boundary words are both deleted and (across neighbours) duplicated; overlapping the windows makes each seam fully interior to a neighbour, which is recoverable by string-overlap stitching since the shared span is re-emitted identically
hypothesis: cut overlapping 30s windows (25s hop), decode all in one batched generate() call, and stitch adjacent texts by removing the longest duplicated char-run at the seam, to eliminate boundary deletions/duplications that plain chunking left

capability_investigated: generate() sequences_ids contents when the prompt omits <|notimestamps|>, and the relation of timestamp token ids to the <|0.00|> base id
what_i_learned: dropping <|notimestamps|> makes the decode interleave timestamp tokens (ids >= convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>")) into sequences_ids at 0.02s resolution; the last such token is a model-chosen segment boundary the stub and the prior seam-stitch attempts were throwing away, which lets the window advance to a real boundary instead of a blind 30s cut
hypothesis: replace the single fixed-window decode with a sequential loop that re-enables timestamps and seeks to the last emitted timestamp each window, eliminating tail deletion past 30s and removing fixed-grid seams entirely (no stitching/dedup needed)

capability_investigated: generate() per-item prompt list — token prefix beyond the fixed [sot,lang,task], specifically <|startofprev|> previous-text conditioning
what_i_learned: the prompt list passed to generate() is arbitrary, so the canonical Whisper prev-text context (<|startofprev|> + prior committed text ids, capped near 224) can be prepended; the prior sequential loop decoded every window context-free, which is consistent with the uniform length_ratio<1.0 deletion signal
hypothesis: prepend the running committed transcript (last 224 ids) after <|startofprev|> to each window's prompt so the decoder has continuation context across seams, recovering deleted/under-emitted speech and lowering corpus_cer

capability_investigated: generate() result object fields beyond sequences_ids, specifically the per-sequence confidence score returned when return_scores=True
what_i_learned: the decode result exposes a per-sequence score (avg log-prob) alongside sequences_ids that the loop was discarding; this score is the signal canonical Whisper uses to detect a degenerate window and trigger temperature fallback
hypothesis: greedy decode (beam_size=1, temp=0) occasionally collapses on hard spans producing the uniform length_ratio<1.0 deletion signal, so score-gate each window and re-decode once at sampling_temperature=0.4 when score < -1.0, recovering dropped text without paying compute on confident windows
